title: TNH September 2024 Class MSN 106 Gastrointestinal Disorders Block One Examination

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs and True/False statements from TNH September 2024 Class MSN 106 Gastrointestinal Disorders Block One Examination paper (sat 3 April 2025, Section A, Q1 to Q30).

questions.text: Histamine in the GIT:
questions.explanation: Stimulates gastric acid secretion (A) is correct because histamine acts on H2 receptors of the parietal cells.

questions.text: Coffee ground vomitus is suggestive of:
questions.explanation: Gastric bleeding (C) is correct because blood is changed to a dark brown colour by gastric acid. Variceal bleeding (A) is bright red.

questions.text: A patient who presents with steatorrhea is likely to have malabsorption of:
questions.explanation: Fats (C) is correct because steatorrhea is fatty stool from malabsorbed fat.

questions.text: Assessment finding on percussion of the right upper abdominal quadrant is:
questions.explanation: Dull sound (C) is correct because the liver is a solid organ in this quadrant. Tympany (A) is over air-filled bowel.

questions.text: McBurney's point tenderness is located at:
questions.explanation: Right lower abdominal quadrant (C) is correct because McBurney's point lies one third of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.

questions.text: An appropriate position for digital rectal examination is:
questions.explanation: Left lateral (C) is correct because Sims' position with knees flexed gives access to the anus and rectum. Right lateral (B) and Trendelenburg (D) are not used. Note: lithotomy (A) may also be used, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Achalasia is caused by degeneration of myenteric plexus.
questions.explanation: True (A) is correct because loss of the inhibitory neurons of the myenteric plexus stops sphincter relaxation and peristalsis.

questions.text: Achalasia is managed by administration of proton pump inhibitors.
questions.explanation: False (B) is correct because PPIs reduce acid but do not relax the sphincter; treatment is by calcium channel blockers, botulinum toxin, dilation or myotomy.

questions.text: A common side effect of barium swallow is:
questions.explanation: Constipation (B) is correct because barium is not absorbed and can harden in the bowel.

questions.text: A condition associated with gastroesophageal reflux disease is:
questions.explanation: Achalasia (D) is correct from the options because it affects the lower esophageal sphincter and reflux commonly occurs after treatment. Pyloric stenosis, appendicitis and cholelithiasis are not related. Note: hiatal hernia is the usual association, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Obesity is a risk factor for gastroesophageal reflux disease because it:

options.C: Tightens the lower oesophageal sphincter muscle

questions.explanation: Increases intra-abdominal pressure (B) is correct because the pressure pushes stomach contents into the esophagus.

questions.text: The most critical immediate postoperative concern a nurse should be on lookout for post oesophagectomy due to oesophageal cancer is:
questions.explanation: Anastomotic leak (B) is correct because leakage causes mediastinitis and sepsis and is life-threatening.

questions.text: A key component of triple therapy in management of chronic gastritis associated with H. Pylori is:

options.A: Proton pump inhibitor and two antibiotics
options.B: NSAIDS, antibiotic and a proton pump inhibitor
options.C: Histamine 2 receptor blocker and two antibiotics
options.D: Antacid, antibiotic and a proton pump inhibitor

questions.explanation: Proton pump inhibitor and two antibiotics (A) is correct, for example a PPI with clarithromycin and amoxicillin.

questions.text: A true statement regarding peptic ulcers is:

options.A: An alternative pain medication in peptic ulcer is diclofenac
options.B: Duodenal ulcers are associated with hunger pains
options.C: Food intake increases pain in duodenal ulcers
options.D: Gastric ulcer is associated with weight gain

questions.explanation: Duodenal ulcers are associated with hunger pains (B) is correct because pain occurs when the stomach is empty and is relieved by food. Diclofenac (A) is an NSAID that causes ulcers, food relieves duodenal pain (C), and gastric ulcer causes weight loss (D).

questions.text: A surgical procedure often combined with vagotomy to prevent gastric stasis is:
questions.explanation: Pyloroplasty (B) is correct because vagotomy delays emptying, and widening the pylorus lets the stomach drain.

questions.text: A classical initial symptom of non-ruptured appendicitis is:

options.A: Sharp left lower quadrant pain radiating to the chest
options.B: Periumbilical pain localized to right lower quadrant

questions.explanation: Periumbilical pain localized to right lower quadrant (B) is correct because pain starts around the umbilicus and migrates.

questions.text: The appropriate nursing intervention for a patient diagnosed with peritonitis is:

options.C: Give cathartics to increase bowel emptying

questions.explanation: Insertion of nasogastric tube (D) is correct for decompression. Oral feeds, oral drugs and cathartics are avoided.

questions.text: The part of colon that is most commonly affected by diverticular diseases is:
questions.explanation: Sigmoid colon (D) is correct because it has the highest intraluminal pressure.

questions.text: In crohn's disease:

options.A: The mucosal lining has cobblestones appearance
options.C: Mucosa and submucosa are affected only

questions.explanation: The mucosal lining has cobblestones appearance (A) is correct. Inflammation is patchy (B), all layers are affected (C) and granulomas are common (D).

questions.text: The major cause of toxic megacolon is:
questions.explanation: Ulcerative colitis (B) is correct because severe inflammation paralyses the colon wall and it dilates.

questions.text: Mechanical causes of intestinal obstruction include:
questions.explanation: Intussusception, fecalith (C) is correct because both are mechanical. The other options each contain a functional cause (paralytic ileus, muscular dystrophy, Parkinson's disease).

questions.text: A pre-procedural lab test that is most important before administration of IV contrast for CT abdomen is:
questions.explanation: Serum creatinine (B) is correct because contrast can damage the kidneys, so renal function is checked first.

questions.text: In left sided colorectal cancer, characteristic of stool include:
questions.explanation: Ribbon shaped stool (B) is correct because the left colon is narrow and the stool is liquid to formed, and the tumour narrows the lumen. Occult bleeding (C) is typical of right-sided cancer.

questions.text: Sclerotherapy in haemorrhoids treatment involves:

options.B: Inducing fibrolysis and collapse of haemorrhoids
options.C: Exposing haemorrhoids to a freezing agent causing collapse
options.D: Using a rubber to ligate haemorrhoids hence necrosis

questions.explanation: Inducing fibrolysis and collapse of haemorrhoids (B) is correct because a sclerosant is injected to cause fibrosis (the paper says fibrolysis). Option A is coagulation, C is cryotherapy and D is rubber band ligation.

questions.text: In acute pancreatitis:

options.B: Patient experience hypoglycaemia followed by hyperglycaemia
options.C: Patient experiences abdominal pains that are relieved by antacids

questions.explanation: Pancreatic lipase is elevated (A) is correct because the damaged gland releases enzymes into the blood. Pain is not relieved by antacids (C), and jaundice can occur (D). Note: the expected answer is A, so check option D against the marking scheme.

questions.text: The main cause of calculous cholecystitis is:
questions.explanation: Bile stones (D) is correct because a stone blocks the cystic duct.

questions.text: A medication used for non-surgical management of small cholesterol gallstones is:
questions.explanation: Ursodiol (B) is correct because bile acids dissolve cholesterol stones.

questions.text: The definitive treatment for refractory portal hypertension is:
questions.explanation: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (A) is correct because a shunt reduces portal pressure. The other options control bleeding.

questions.text: Collateral circulation in portal hypertension:

options.A: Directs blood flow from arteries to veins
options.B: Is the formation of an alternative vascular pathway in response to obstruction
options.C: Is a congenital malformation of blood vessels in response to obstruction
options.D: Occurs to shunt blood from the obstruction to the brain tissues

questions.explanation: Is the formation of an alternative vascular pathway in response to obstruction (B) is correct.

questions.text: In ascites:

options.A: The patient is advised to increase food rich in sodium
options.B: Low albumin in blood is a predisposing factor

questions.explanation: Low albumin in blood is a predisposing factor (B) is correct because low oncotic pressure lets fluid leak into the abdomen.

questions.text: The types of hepatitis transmitted through faecal oral route are:
questions.explanation: A, E (A) is correct because hepatitis A and E are spread through contaminated food and water.
